description: Registry of all AdCP JSON schemas for validation and discovery

versioning.note: AdCP uses path-based versioning. The schema URL path (/schemas/) indicates the version. Individual request/response schemas do NOT include adcp_version fields. Compatibility follows semantic versioning rules.

Declares the SOURCE of feature evaluation via one of two forms (inline pass/fail exemplars calibrating a single predicted_performance feature, or an external get_creative_features-capable agent_url), an optional hard feature_requirement[] GATE (drop fails — internal best_of_n pruning), an explicit rank_by ordering ({feature_id, direction}), an allowlisted feature_agent pointer (accepted_verifiers; off-list → EVALUATOR_AGENT_NOT_ACCEPTED), plus an optional soft eval_budget. Informs best_of_n recommended/rank; never blocks an already-produced billable leaf.

format-revision.description: Semantic version of a community format entry's input contract in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH form.

trust.description: EXPERIMENTAL (identity.trust_json): agent trust record format specification, schemas only. Nothing in AdCP 3.3 reads, requires, or verifies it, and the document name and path may change before graduation. See RFC #7809.
trust.purpose: Declares the agents an organization runs and their keys, the authority it delegates, and the grants it accepts. The file location is provisional and may change before graduation. Protocol-neutral core with namespaced roles and scopes; AdCP is the first profile. Not consumed by any AdCP 3.3 behavior.

trust-acknowledgements.description: Bulk acknowledgements sub-document referenced from trust.json acknowledgements_url (experimental)

trusted-match.description: Trusted Match Protocol (TMP) — real-time execution layer for activating pre-negotiated packages across any surface. Conformance invariants are normative in docs/trusted-match/specification.mdx; the cap-fire boundary contract is at docs/trusted-match/identity-match-implementation.mdx; a non-normative impression-tracker implementation reference (multi-identity dedup, fcap_keys labels, log-based data model, SDK primitives) is at docs/trusted-match/impression-tracker-implementation.mdx. Storage backend is an implementation choice; conformant services may use any store that satisfies the invariants.

available-package.description: A package available for contextual matching on a given impression opportunity

offer.description: Buyer's response to a context match — ranges from simple activation (package_id only) to rich offers with brand, price, summary, and creative manifest

error.description: Error response from a TMP provider or router when a request cannot be processed

provider-registration.description: TMP provider registration — endpoint, capabilities, and operational parameters for router configuration

provider-context-match-response.description: Provider-to-router Context Match response shape — carries provider-local targeting key-values and forbids router-authored attribution buckets

provider-identity-match-response.description: Provider-to-router Identity Match response shape — carries ordered TMPX `{slot_id, value}` chunks with no publisher-local names

publisher-targeting-kv-config.description: Publisher-owned deployment configuration that maps (provider_id, provider-local targeting key) to the ad-server targeting destination for that surface

publisher-tmpx-config.description: Publisher-owned deployment configuration that maps (provider_id, slot_id) to the ad-server macro name, GAM key-value, VAST substitution, or play-log field for that surface

tmpx-chunk.description: A single TMPX chunk — provider-local slot_id and opaque URL-safe value; shared between provider→router and router→publisher hops

request.description: Evaluate available packages against content context. Contains no user identity.

response.description: Router-to-publisher offers for matched packages with provider-attributed targeting signals

request.description: Evaluate user eligibility for packages using an opaque identity token. Contains no page context.

response.description: Per-package eligibility — boolean eligible plus optional intent score

brand-protocol.description: Brand protocol for identity retrieval, rights discovery, acquisition, and lifecycle management

rights-terms.description: Terms returned with a rights grant — coverage, restrictions, revocation, and credentials

creative-approval-request.description: Payload the buyer submits to the approval_webhook from acquire_rights for rights-holder creative review

creative-approval-response.description: Response from the approval_webhook — approved, rejected, or pending_review

revocation-notification.description: Notification sent to the buyer's revocation_webhook when an acquired rights grant is revoked

verification-status.description: Shared status enum returned by verify_brand_claim — owned, pending_review, transferring, disputed, not_ours, archived, licensed_in, licensed_out, unknown

request.description: Request parameters for retrieving brand identity data from a brand agent
Request parameters for verifying a single brand claim (subsidiary / parent / property / trademark, discriminated by claim_type)

response.description: Response payload for verify_brand_claim task — claim_type echoed, status from the shared VerificationStatus enum, per-claim-type details

request.description: Request parameters for bulk verification — claims[] array (max 100), each entry shaped like a single verify_brand_claim request

response.description: Response payload for verify_brand_claims task — results[] positionally aligned with the request's claims[], per-result success or error inline

request.description: Request parameters for searching licensable rights with pricing
Request parameters for acquiring rights with contractual clearance

response.description: Response payload for acquire_rights task — terms and generation credentials

request.description: Request parameters for modifying an active rights grant — dates, caps, pricing, or pause/resume

extensions.description: Typed extension schemas for vendor-specific or domain-specific data. Extensions define the structure of data within the ext.{namespace} field. Agents declare which extensions they support in their agent card.

registry.description: Auto-generated registry of all available extensions with metadata

meta.description: Schema that all extension files must follow. Defines valid_from, valid_until, and extension data structure.

compliance.description: Compliance testing tool schemas. The test controller is an optional sandbox-only tool that lets comply walk full lifecycle state machines by triggering seller-side transitions deterministically.

task-completion-data.description: Bounded force_task_completion result union for supported legacy async scenarios

request.description: Request payload for the comply_test_controller tool — scenario selection and scenario-specific params

response.description: Response payload — state transition results, simulation results, scenario list, or structured errors

usage.validation: Use these schemas to validate AdCP requests and responses
usage.codeGeneration: Generate client SDKs using these schemas
